# The Author’s Report,
## How he found this path to Christ and walked upon it himself.
### An extract from his twelfth Epistle <note>original: *Send-Brief*, a formal letter intended for circulation among spiritual followers</note>.

May the open fountain-spring in the heart of Jesus Christ <note>original: *JEsu Christi*</note> be our refreshment, and lead us into Himself, so that we may live in His power, rejoice in Him, love, know, and enter into one will.

<margin>The author, as a child,</margin>
I shall not hide from you the simple path of a child which I walk in Christ. For I can write of myself in no other way than as of a child who knows and understands nothing, and has never learned anything, except only this: what the Lord wishes to know within me, according to the measure in which He reveals Himself in me.

# Preface.

...hiddenness in my spirit showed this sufficiently / for what end it might be / yet outer reason <term>reason</term> <note>original: *Vernunft*. In Böhme's context, this refers to human logic and worldly intellectual effort, which he often contrasts with divine revelation.</note> was always the opposite <note>original: *Contrarium*. A Latin term meaning the polar opposite or adversary.</note>: Except only at times / when the **Morning Star** <note>original: *Morgenstern*. A symbol for the dawning of divine light or Christ's presence within the human soul.</note> rose / then was reason also ignited / and danced along / as if it had grasped it / but it is far from it.

<margin>God dwells in the likeness.</margin>
**God** dwells in the noble likeness <note>original: *Bildniß*. This refers to the "image of God" (imago Dei) within a person, which Böhme believes is the only place where God can truly reside in a human being.</note> / and not in the spirit of the stars and elements; He possesses nothing / but only Himself in His own kind. And although He does possess Something / as He then possesses Everything / yet nothing grasps Him / except only that / which has sprung and come from Him / such as the soul in the likeness of **God**.

<margin>It is a student’s writing,</margin>
Therefore all my writing is like that of a student / who goes to school; **God** has led my soul into a wondrous school / and I can in truth claim nothing for myself / as if my "I-hood" <term>I-hood</term> <note>original: *Ichheit*. A term Böhme uses to describe the self-centered ego or the "self" that acts independently of God’s will.</note> were anything or understood anything.

<margin>the work is God’s.</margin>
No one should think more highly of me / than he sees here: For the work in my labor is not mine / I have it only according to the measure / as it is granted to me by the **Lord**; I am only His tool / with which He does / what He wills. I report this...

## Preface. 10

<margin>
Reason judges the other from the outside; the Spirit of **God** from the inside.
</margin>
Who can judge divine matters if the Spirit of the Lord is not within them? The Spirit of the Lord alone judges and examines all things: For to Him alone all things are known and manifest. Human reason, however, judges from the outside, and one person's reason always judges according to another’s: the small according to the great, the layman according to the <term>doctor</term> <note>original: *Doctor*. In Böhme’s time, this specifically referred to a highly educated academic or a Doctor of Divinity.</note>. Thus, no one grasps the truth or the Lord’s mind except for the Spirit of God, which judges within the human being and is no respecter of persons <note>a biblical phrase meaning God does not show favoritism based on social status or rank</note>: to Him, the layman is the same as the doctor.

<margin>
Conflict over the letter has grown out of the diverse gifts of the children of God.
</margin>
But because the children of **God** have such a variety of gifts for writing, speaking, and judging, and do not all follow the same style, one’s own reason thereafter sucks out its own profit and creates a **Babel** <note>Böhme uses "Babel" to represent the confusion, sectarianism, and prideful intellectualism of the organized church of his day.</note>. From this, so many different opinions have arisen, as people have devised their own views and "ways to God" out of those holy writings—insisting on which paths one ought to walk. Thus, such a quarrel has arisen that, at present, man looks only upon the dispute, seeing who can overcome the other through an exchange of letters <note>original: *Buchstaben-Wechseln*. This refers to pedantic arguments over the literal text of scripture or academic definitions rather than spiritual experience.</note>. That is all **Babel**, a mother of spiritual harlotry <note>a common 17th-century metaphor for the corruption of the church through human pride and false doctrines</note>, where reason does not enter through the door of Christ, through Christ’s Spirit into the

foolish.

## How we must seek again that which was lost, etc.

# Preface.

God wrestled. <note>Böhme frequently invokes the image of Jacob wrestling the angel (Genesis 32) as a metaphor for the soul's intense internal struggle to overcome doubt and reach God.</note> Even if your conscience says a resounding "No"—that God does not want you—I nonetheless want Him; I will not let go of You until they carry me to the grave; my will be Your will; I want what You, Lord, want. ## A brief indication of the key to the understanding of Divine Mystery / how man may attain Divine Contemplation within himself.

---

Whosoever wishes to attain to Divine Contemplation <term>contemplation: "Beschaulichkeit," a state of quiet, prayerful observation of the divine presence within the soul.</term> within himself / and to speak with God in Christ / let him follow this process, and so he shall arrive at it.

<margin>Man should take up a serious intent,</margin>
1. # On Holy Prayer/

## Toward Every Day of the Week.

How a person should constantly remember their **calling** <term>calling: the German *Amt* refers to one's specific duty, professional role, or office as ordained by God</term> / station / and conduct / in which God has placed them : and how they should entrust their beginning / middle / and end in all their deeds to God / and always perform all their works with God ; just as the branch of a tree produces its twigs with the power of the root / and bears its fruit upon them : and how they should draw strength from God’s small fountain for all their workings at every beginning / and thank their Creator for every good deed.

### Alongside Heartfelt Contemplation of the Suffering / Death and Resurrection of JEsus Christ.

How a person should always lead the hunger and desire of their soul through the death of Christ into His resurrection in God / and press toward the new **rebirth**; so that they may pray in spirit and in truth / and that the Spirit of Christ may pray in and with them / and intercede for them before God.

# The Author’s Preface to the God-loving Reader.
## On the True Foundation of the Right Art of Prayer / What Prayer Is / and Why God Commands Us to Pray.

<margin>Prayer is not merely an ordinary speaking of words.</margin>
Dear Christian reader! Praying rightly is not merely a habit / such that one need only speak the words of prayer: No; such speaking of words / without heartfelt devotion and divine desire / is only an external thing / an external formation of words.

<margin>The mouth only creates a form of the will without power</margin>
2. The mouth forms its words of prayer with the external power of the stars <term>stars: in seventeenth-century mysticism, the *Gestirne* or stars refer to the astrological and natural forces that govern physical existence</term> and the elements / and creates only a form of the will / in which there is no actual power. For nothing pleases God / except what He Himself works and does through a thing. <note>The author suggests that true prayer is a divine act happening *through* the person, rather than a human performance.</note>

<margin>about which God complains through the Prophet.</margin>
3. For God complains through the Prophet about such external mouth-prayer without power / when He says: "They draw near to me with their lips / but their heart is far from me," Isaiah 29:13. Likewise / Christ says: "Not all / who say: Lord, Lord! shall enter into the kingdom of heaven / but those who do the will—"

<meta>catchword: will—</meta>

<summary>This preface introduces the "art of prayer," emphasizing that true prayer must come from a heart filled with divine desire rather than being a mechanical recitation of words. The author argues that empty prayers lack spiritual power because they are driven by physical nature rather than God's spirit.</summary>

> O **Lord Jesus Christ** / clothe me in the garment of your innocence / in which you / while wearing our garment / took upon yourself the scorn of all people. ## Chapter 2.

<margin>The resigned will makes a perfect work.</margin>
Whoever intends to work something perfect and good / in which he hopes to rejoice eternally / and to enjoy it / let him go out of <term>Selfhood</term> <note>Selbheit: the state of being centered on one's own ego and selfish desires</note> / as his own desire / and enter into <term>Resignation</term> <note>Gelassenheit: a central concept meaning the surrendering of one's personal will to the divine will</note> in God's will / and work with God.

<margin>And breaks the essence of selfhood.</margin>
2. Even if the earthly desire of selfhood clings to him in flesh and blood / as long as the soul-will does not embrace it / then selfhood may produce no work. For the resigned will breaks the essence of selfhood ever again / so that the wrath of God may not reach it: And even if it does reach it / which is not entirely impossible / and may happen / the resigned will nevertheless carries its power upward within it / so it stands in the figure before God / as a work of victory in wonder / and may inherit the divine sonship.

<margin>It is not good to speak while reason is ignited in the desire of selfhood.</margin>
3. Therefore it is not good to speak or act / when <term>reason</term> <note>Vernunft: here referring to human intellect or logic when it is separated from divine illumination</note> is ignited in the desire of selfhood; that desire works otherwise in God's wrath / from which the person will suffer harm / for his work is brought into God's wrath / and kept until the great Day of Judgment of God.

### IV. OF THE MENTAL LIFE. <note>original: "DE VITA MENTALI"; Böhme uses this title to refer to the inner life of the mind and spirit, often translated as the "Supersensual Life."</note>

18. **The Disciple said:** How would it be for him, though, if God’s <term>wrath</term> <note>original: "Zorn"; in Böhme’s theology, this is not just anger, but the "dark fire" or the harsh, stern principle of nature that must be transformed by Divine Love.</note> attacked him from within, and the evil world from without, as happened to our Lord Christ? **The Master said:** It would happen to him as it did to our Lord Christ. ### V. On Regeneration. Preface.
<note>original: "V. De Regeneratione. Præf."</note>

—one's understanding is not sufficient to grasp; therefore, I have written a short <term>summary</term> <note>original: "Summam"</note> of the new birth <term>New Birth: Also known as regeneration, this is the spiritual transformation where a person is reborn through divine grace rather than physical nature.</term> for the service of the simple children of Christ and at the request of good friends, to see if anyone might wish to learn to recognize themselves through it.

...ly: He speaks one way and acts another, and testifies that his mouth is a liar; for what he teaches, he does not do himself, and serves only the **animalistic man** <term>animalistic man: *tierischen Menschen*, a term used to describe the unregenerate human state driven by earthly desires and "vanity" rather than the Spirit</term> in vanity.

<margin>External comfort does not help.</margin>
8. For if someone says: "I have the will, and would gladly do good, but I have earthly flesh which holds me back so that I cannot; but I shall be saved by grace for the sake of **Christ’s merit** <term>merit: *Verdienst*, the spiritual value of Christ's sacrifice applied to the believer</term>; for I indeed comfort myself in His suffering and merit; He will accept me by grace without any merit of my own and forgive my sin"—such a person acts exactly like one who knew of a good food for his health and did not eat it, but instead ate a poisonous one in its place, from which he became sick and died.

<margin>Knowledge also does not help.</margin>
9. What does it help the soul to know the way to God and yet not wish to walk it, but instead walks the path of error and does not reach God? Certainly and truly, this tickling and flattering of oneself with Christ’s merit, outside of the true, inborn childhood, is false and a lie, let whoever will teach it.

# Chapter 6.

Dear brothers, we want to speak faithfully with you, not from a hypocritical mouth to please the Antichrist, but from our little pearl <note>original: *Perlein*, a common mystical metaphor for the divine spark or wisdom within the soul</note>, from Christian essence and knowledge; not from the husk and histories <term>histories: *Historien*, referring to a purely intellectual or historical belief in scripture without personal spiritual experience</term>; but from a childlike spirit, from Christ’s knowledge, as a branch on the vine of Christ, from the measure of that knowledge revealed within us in God’s counsel.

<margin>Temple of Christ.</margin>
2. People bind us now to histories, to stone churches, which would indeed be good in their value if one also brought the temple of Christ into them.

<margin>Absolution. The Lord's Supper.</margin>
3. They teach that their absolution is a forgiveness of sins; likewise, that the Lord’s Supper <note>original: *Abendmahl*, literally "Evening Meal"</note> takes away sins; likewise, that the Spirit of God is poured in through the office of preaching.

## Chapter 1.
### What **GOD** is: And how one should recognize His Divine Being through His Revelation.

Reason says: I hear much said of **GOD**, that there is a **GOD** who created all things, and also sustains and carries all things; but I have not yet seen anyone, nor heard of anyone, who has seen **GOD**, or who could sa- <note>The text breaks here to continue on the next page; the full word is "sagen" or "say."</note>

<header>VI. <term>THEOSCOPIA</term>. Chapter 1.</header>

-say: where **GOD** dwells or is, or what He is like. For when Reason beholds the essence of this world and considers how the godly person fares the same as the wicked; and how all things are mortal and fragile; also how the godly see no savior who delivers them from the anguish and adversity of the wicked, and thus must descend to the grave in misery with great anxiety; so it thinks all things happen by chance. It thinks there is no **GOD** who takes care of the suffering, because He lets the one who hopes in Him remain stuck in misery and descend into the grave; and one has also heard of no one who has come back from decay and said he had been with **GOD**.

<margin>Reason cannot behold **GOD**.</margin>
2. Answer. Reason is a natural life, whose foundation <note>original: "Grund." In this context, it refers to the underlying basis or origin of a being's existence.</note> stands in a temporal beginning and end, and it cannot enter into the supernatural foundation in which **GOD** is understood. For even though Reason gazes upon itself in this world and finds no other foundation in its contemplation, it nevertheless feels within itself a desire for a higher foundation in which it might find rest:

<margin>Reason feels a desire for rest.</margin>

It desires to rest in that which is not subject to suffering, and seeks rest in that which it is not within itself. It desires the death of its selfhood <note>original: "Ichheit." A central concept in this philosophy, referring to the ego or the "I" that is separated from God.</note>, and yet it does not desire to become a "nothing"; rather, it only desires to die away from its torment so that it may rest within itself.

5. It surrenders itself to suffering so that the power of its own painful state might kill its suffering. It hopes that through the death of its "dying to self" <note>original: "Selbsterbens." 6. In this, one rightly understands the hidden **GOD**: how He reveals Himself in the <term>mind</term> <note>original: "Gemühte." 7. Reason asks: Why has God created a life of painful suffering? Could it not exist in a better state without suffering and torment, since He is the ground and beginning of all things? Why does He endure this <term>opposition</term> <note>original: "Widerwillen," meaning a resistance or a contrary will.</note>? <margin>
Without contrariness, nothing can be revealed to itself;
</margin>

8. Answer: No thing can be revealed to itself without <term>contrariness</term> <note>original: "Widerwärtigkeit." For if it has nothing that resists it, it always proceeds outward and never returns back into itself. But if it does not return into itself—as into that source from which it originally came—then it knows nothing of its own <term>original state</term> <note>original: "Urstand." This refers to the primal foundation or the beginning of a thing's existence in God.</note>.

<margin>
Nor sensitive.
</margin>

### A highly precious gateway, well worth the God-loving reader's contemplation.

The fierce devil has a mighty entrance into it, for the <term>fire-property</term> <note>Böhme views fire as a "harsh" quality associated with the Father's wrath when not tempered by the Light of the Son.</note> serves him. He is also proud and envious, and so is this <term>temperament</term>. O, how difficult it is for the soul to get free when it is truly ignited in this quality! O devil in the form of an angel, how dark you will be when the temperament breaks apart in death!

# VIII. ON THE FOUR TEMPERAMENTS <note>original Latin: "De Quatuor Complexionibus."</note>

### 3. The Phlegmatic Temperament according to Water.

<margin>Phlegmatic</margin>
29. If the **soul** is surrounded by this <term>temperament</term> <note>original: "Complexion." In the humoral theory used by Böhme, this refers to the Phlegmatic disposition, associated with the element of water.</note> and blows forth its life from it, it is a thick, swollen life—clumsy, lazy, base, and dismissive. It possesses a coarse body and poor reason; yet, through teaching, all common worldly matters can be introduced into it. If the power of the **Moon** does not intervene, it is quite a coarse block; furthermore, it is rendered nearly unjust through the power of the Moon.

<margin>Accepts everything.</margin>
30. One can carve all manner of things out of this temperament; the **water-spirit** accepts everything—now evil, now good. Water is deceptive <note>original: "scheinlicht," implying something that gleams or has a false appearance.</note>; the soul also does not easily become aware of God’s wrath and the dark world (which is at its center). It bites greedily at the abominations of the world and hides them under the shimmer of the water, in the belief that it is God’s brilliance.

# On Spiritual Conflict Arising from Temperament and the Stars.

<margin>Spiritual conflict does not all come from the devil.</margin>
64. Spiritual conflict <note>original: "Anfechtung." This term describes a state of deep spiritual trial, doubt, or "assault" on the soul's faith.</note> does not always come from the devil (especially in melancholic people); most sadness comes from the soul's own imagination when it must dwell in a melancholic "inn" <note>lodging or physical body</note>. There, the soul easily becomes sad and thinks God has forgotten it, or that He does not want it. For the melancholic temperament is dark and has no light of its own like the others; yet it does not belong to the inner essence of the soul. During this time of outer life, it is merely the soul's dwelling-house. Likewise, the soul's holiness and righteousness do not reside in the temperament, but in heaven with God: For St. Paul says (Philippians 3:20): *Our citizenship is in heaven.* <note>original: "Unser Wandel ist im Himmel." Böhme translates the Latin/Greek concept of citizenship or "conversation" as one's habitual way of being.</note> This heaven, where God dwells, is not manifest within the temperament, but within itself in the <term>second Principle: original "andern Principio." In Böhme's system, this represents the realm of light and divine love, distinct from the dark fire or the physical world.</term>

<margin>The most holy souls can often become sad.</margin>
65. For if Christ is to live in the person, then the self's own <term>spirit of lust</term> <note>original: "Lust-Geist"; the driving force of worldly desire and pleasure-seeking.</note> must die. And although it does not die completely in this lifetime because of the flesh, but rather dies daily and yet lives: this is the reason for such a struggle, which no godless person feels, but only those who have "put on Christ," in whom Christ fights with Lucifer.

<margin>The third temptation stands in the will and mind, as well as in flesh and blood.</margin>
16. The third trial consists in the devil’s robber-castles—that is, in the will and the <term>mind</term> <note>original: "Gemühte"; the deep-seated emotional and spiritual disposition of the soul.</note>, as well as in flesh and blood—where the <term>false centers</term> <note>original: "falsche Centra"; the Latin "centra" refers to the focal points of the soul's energy that are misaligned with God.</note> lie within the human being. These include the self-will toward a proud, temporal life, toward the lust of the flesh, and toward earthly things; likewise, many curses of men which have been wished upon his body and soul through his temptation. All sins, which have centered themselves and stand in the <term>spirit-constellation</term> <note>original: "Geist-Gestirne"; Böhme's concept that the human spirit has its own internal "astronomy" or arrangement of forces mirroring the stars.</note> as a firm castle, are what Christ is now storming and wishes to break apart. The human will still continually regards this castle of its own power, pleasure, and the beauty of this world as its own property and its best interest, and does not want to surrender and obey Christ.

**20.** Therefore I say: if someone is a Christian, he is not so through a veneer of grace <note>original: "Gnaden-Schein." <meta>This page follows the alphabetical index of Jacob Böhme’s works and appears to be a concluding pastoral exhortation or a summary of the mystical path described in the preceding texts. It focuses on the shift from external ritual to an "inward faith" where the presence of Christ is experienced within the soul rather than as an external historical figure.</meta>

Therefore, all my brothers and sisters in Christ <note>original: "Christo" — the Latin dative form of Christus.</note>, because we should now, through our **inward faith**, have such boldness <note>original: "freidigkeit" — a term often used in older German bibles to denote the confidence or "freeness" with which a believer approaches God.</note> and entrance to the holy **cleansing blood** of the **crucified one**, which He has also prepared for us as the new and living way, and toward the **new creature** <note>original: "Creatur" — in this context, referring to the "new creation" or "new man" mentioned in Pauline theology, the spiritual rebirth of the individual.</note> in His own flesh; and as we now have a true **high priest** over the **house of God**, let us then go forth with a single and true heart, with our sorrowful, **inward faith of repentance** <note>original: "buß glauben" — a faith born from "Busse," meaning both repentance and the internal process of turning away from the self toward God.</note>, sprinkled with love in our hearts, free from evil thoughts, and washed clean in body. 

We should also hold right fast to the true **knowledge** and confession of God and the certain hope, so that we do not waver or retreat from it, but rather rely confidently on His Word of God. For He Himself has said: "I will not leave you, nor forsake you, as long as you keep faithfulness and faith." We Christians should also kindly entice and stir one another toward Christian love and good works, so that our **inward faith** becomes beautifully perfect, that we may endure. 

Blessed is he who recognizes this light, also in spirit and truth, with his **inward faith**. He also belongs to those who say: "We are not of those who retreat, but of those who hold fast in inward faith," specifically Jesus the crucified **in us**, and not **outside of us**. In us, He makes us righteous and blessed <note>original: "seelig" — meaning both saved and filled with divine bliss.</note>. May God, by His grace, grant this to me and to all my brothers and sisters to enjoy, here in **temporality** <note>original: "Zeitigkeit" — refers to our time-bound, earthly existence.</note>, and there in **eternity**.

->Whoever now truly believes<-
->becomes blessed. Amen.<-

<summary>This concluding exhortation encourages believers to seek a direct, internal relationship with the "crucified Christ within," emphasizing inward repentance and faith over external forms. It promises that through this internal presence, one finds both righteousness and eternal bliss.</summary>

<keywords>inward faith, cleansing blood, high priest, new creature, repentance, Christ within, temporality, eternity, salvation</keywords>
